anomalies.observed: Both UART3 connector signal lines are tied to FCC1 pins that the library defines as VCAP (power_out, the internal core-regulator decoupling pins). UART3_TX_FCC sits on pin 48 and UART3_RX_FCC on pin 73. The MCU's USART3 candidate pins PD8 (pin 55) and PD9 (pin 56) are not used for this connector: PD8 is unconnected and PD9 is on GPIO_A_FCC.
anomalies.expected: The VCAP pins must connect only to their external decoupling capacitors (to GND). UART3 signals belong on dedicated USART pins, not on a power-output pin of the core regulator.
anomalies.impact: The UART3 lines are driven onto, or shorted to, the internal core-regulator output, so UART3 will not communicate and the core supply decoupling is compromised. The FCC-side connector's serial link to peripherals is non-functional.

anomalies.observed: The LD39200 3.3 V LDO output is on net '+3.3V' (with the sensors, EEPROM, flash and GPS). The MCU decoupling, I2C pull-ups and the NAVC/FCC supply pins sit on a separate net named '+3V3'. No part bridges the two, so the MCU/peripheral 3V3 rail has no source on the netlist.
anomalies.expected: The LDO output and the MCU/peripheral 3V3 rail must be one net, as the spec says the LDO powers 'MCUs and Sensors'.

evidence.quote: 3.3 V LDO (MCUs + sensors) | Hades (top sheet) | ST LD39200PU33R

anomalies.impact: If the nets are truly separate, the MCUs and their I2C pull-ups receive no 3.3 V supply. If they are merged elsewhere, this is a naming inconsistency that could hide a real break.
